name: Intraday time-series momentum — 4h low-churn continuation (fee-hurdle stress test)
rationale: MECHANISM: the intraday time-series momentum lead-lag (early-window sign predicts the later-window sign via late-informed traders and end-of-window rebalancing) expressed on a 4h bar. The 1h version is thin and fee-dominated; moving to 4h is the deliberate fee-hurdle experiment — fewer, larger continuation trades so the per-trade move can actually exceed ~3x round-trip taker cost. Entry: positive signed trailing ret_Nd gated by adx (directional regime) with a range_position confirm that price sits in the upper part of its recent range (the continuation is into strength, not a dead-cat within a range). DISCONFIRMER: kill if the 4h net edge is still < 3x round-trip taker cost (then the whole family is a fee mirage, not a timeframe issue), if the adx gate adds nothing, or if the signed lead-lag vanishes in a purged/embargoed OOS split (in-sample fit).
catalyst: coarse-bar early momentum persisting into the later window
